thread:
maria chen: Heads up — after the 1.30 upgrade in eu-west-1 we saw a burst of GPU node launches. Autoscaler kept adding whole nodepools for ~30m. Cost alert firing now.
lee park: Which signal is autoscaler using? capacity or allocatable?
maria chen: Not sure yet, but pods were Pending with '0/1 nvidia.com/gpu' while nodes showed capacity 1. Allocatable went to 0 intermittently.
rachel kim: Sounds like device-plugin restart race. Did kubelet re-register? Any device-plugin logs?
maria chen: I grabbed this quickly:
```
$ kubectl get nodes -o wide | egrep 'gpu'
gpu-node-1   Ready,SchedulingDisabled   1        25d   10.0.3.12
gpu-node-2   Ready                      0        2m    10.0.3.13
```
and
```
$ kubectl describe node gpu-node-2 | sed -n '1,40p'
Capacity:
  cpu:  32
  memory: 124Gi
  nvidia.com/gpu: 1
Allocatable:
  cpu: 30
  memory: 120Gi
  nvidia.com/gpu: 0
```
maria chen: device-plugin pod on that node had restarted right after kubelet updated status (logs show device plugin re-register), so allocatable dropped to 0 briefly and autoscaler treated node as incapable -> scaled up new nodes.
tom gonzalez: Ugh. Autoscaler using a snapshot of capacity/allocatable at evaluation time might be reading capacity first and deciding node not ready, then adding nodes. We saw similar but not identical before.
lee park: Can you paste the device-plugin logs? curious if it returned 'No devices found' during init.
maria chen: logs snippet:
```
I0318 14:12:03.123456 1 plugin.go:231] starting device plugin
E0318 14:12:03.123500 1 plugin.go:245] no devices discovered (nvidia-smi returned non-zero)
I0318 14:12:04.200000 1 plugin.go:312] registered 1 device(s)
```
rachel kim: So 1-2s of 'no devices' then register. But autoscaler decisions happen on a 30s cadence -> the transient 0 allocatable window is long enough.
billing-bot: ALERT: eu-west-1 GPU spend +420% over baseline in last 40m (trigger: cost/surge/high).
ops-bot: Deployments impacted: realtime-infer (3 pods pending), batch-worker (6 pods rescheduled).
lee park: Short-term mitigation: add a small grace debounce before autoscaler treats a node as lacking GPUs. Maybe treat nodes with capacity>0 and transient allocatable==0 as 'provisioning' for 60s.
tom gonzalez: I can put up a tiny autoscaler patch to prefer allocatable but tolerate brief allocatable==0 if capacity>0 and node age < 5m. Will open PR and test.
mar ia chen: Meanwhile i'll roll device-plugin DaemonSet in eu-west-1 to force clean joins. Command I ran:
```
kubectl -n kube-system rollout restart ds/gpu-device-plugin-daemonset --namespace=kube-system
```
lee park: Also recommend changing node bootstrapping to wait for device-plugin readiness before marking node Ready? Might be trickier.
rachel kim: We should record this as upgrade-induced race in the upgrade notes. Action items: 1) Tom PR for autoscaler tolerance; 2) Ops: follow device-plugin restart procedure; 3) Platform: add cost guardrail (auto-throttle) for GPU pool bursts.
lee park: Can we add a short-term policy to force max surge per minute for GPU pool via cluster-autoscaler flags? or throttle cloud provider API?
tom gonzalez: I'll prototype flag --gpu-provisioning-debounce=60s in PR  (WIP): https://stash.redwood/example/pr/1234 (will update).
maria chen: After rolling device-plugin DS, allocatable stabilized and autoscaler scaled back down. Cost alert resolved but we'll keep watch.
ops-bot: Resolved: realtime-infer pods scheduled, batch-worker back to normal.
rachel kim: Postmortem scheduled in #incidents for tomorrow 10:00 UTC. Please add logs and kubelet/device-plugin timings.
maria chen: noted — I'll upload kubelet + device-plugin dumps to the incident thread and include the node age vs allocatable timeline. Thanks all :thumbsup:
